open_points: Clock: every figure in this file that depends on a game-time-to-real-time ratio is listed in clock_figures with old and new. All game-time figures (2 game minutes, 22 words, windows in game hours) are unchanged; only their real-second equivalents move.

Names: the prototype's rent went to Sylvia Rennison. Canon and RT-16 say rent is owed to the landlord's agent, a named man who calls at the counter, and Agar's agents hold the parade; the texts say 'Agar's rent man'. Sylvia Rennison keeps Regent House (people.json) and is not the landlord. The blueprint leaves the agent's name open; letters-and-print.json mints Mr Leonard Askew (chosen).

Story: signs and open items marked story_check (the licence hearing, the Customs morning items, the other-book line, the pen laid on the book) follow the blueprint's mechanics; the frame in production/lane/story/frame/ is a draft (due 26 Nov). The keeper re-checks them against it.

Prototype names that are not in the frozen map or canon cast and were kept as ordinary fictional names: Portside Cars and Len Wardle (the other firm on the north rank), PC Ibbotson. Shaun Hewson's lock-up for the respray is not on the map.

The prototype's debt book is Iveson 80, Darren 22, Wayne 30, Lee 15, Julie 9 (total 156 pounds, matching blueprint 3.1.1). ECONOMY-DESIGN-2026-11-26 section 4 quotes 'Darren still owes 12': taken as a part payment, so the first-week figure stays 22.

Kinds: the prototype has 111 kinds (kinds.js plus game/kinds/*.js); five new ids are added for the 24 Nov decisions (snooker_frame, fished, flew_pigeons, bought_back, struck_down) and marked chosen. The Tom wording of every kind is the prototype's 'mine' text; the truth wording is the prototype's 'truth' text, with rent_paid, rent_late, ellis_asked and talk_ellis changed to canon.

Slot texts: the prototype has no slot wording, only a witness's whole-act belief. The 116 x 7 slot texts are new, written by category with per-kind overrides, all chosen; null means the kind has no such slot (a noise has no victim).
Seven slots follow BLUEPRINT-02 2.2.1. The five-rung identification ladder is held in people_recognition_lines; the rung itself is the town's, never the Ledger's.
The takeaway (Peter and Lily Tang) and the Tivoli are in the cast and canon but not on the frozen map; their cards and open items use no map place id.
The sign list has 45 entries against the sweep's 'about 40'; the three crew signs come from tune/crew.js and the stage signs from tune/law.js.
